name: Kamal Adham

summary.text: Kamal Adham was a former head of Saudi intelligence and, according to the Washington Post, a key figure in the 1982 takeover of First American Bankshares by investors later found to have been fronting for BCCI. In July 1992 he pleaded guilty in New York to violating the state bank holding company act and agreed to pay $105 million to settle charges that he knew First American was illegally controlled, in a plea negotiated by Manhattan District Attorney Robert Morgenthau's office.

openQuestions: The Senate Foreign Relations Committee report's own treatment of Adham (his role as a CCAH shareholder and nominee for BCCI) was not retrieved this session; the connection to BCCI itself is therefore left to the First American item above rather than asserted directly.

A peoplepill.com biography says the $105 million was a joint payment with Sayed Al Jawhary and that Adham was barred from the finance sector; neither detail was confirmed in the contemporaneous reporting.
